description: Measure, on the merged post-#506 model, the same two quantities the expedition campaign measured (expedition_posting_v2: how often a voyage reaches the VSP reporting threshold, and the reported passenger attack rate among the voyages that do) on the two mid-size hulls, classic_cruise_1900 (1,910 berths) and spirit_cruise_3000 (3,000 berths). Complements are the hulls' own declarations, not a table in the manifest. The expedition result this follows up on: posting stopped being a ceiling and became a rate (9 per 1,000 seven-day voyages at the shipped rung, 54 per 1,000 at twelve days), but it departed from the observed pattern in two ways -- the voyage-length gradient was far too shallow (observed passenger-channel posting rises 0.33 to 18.3 per 1,000 from the 6-7 to the 11-14 day band, a factor near 55; the model rose 6 to 37, a factor near 6), and the attack rate conditional on posting was too low (median 0.0348 against A4's 0.0532) with postings clustered on the threshold rather than growing. Neither departure can be attributed to the transmission chain or to the hull while only one hull has been measured: a 450-berth expedition vessel is the smallest, most mixed, least compartmented platform in the fleet, and both the A9 fleet denominator and the A4 median are dominated by hulls this size and larger. This campaign therefore repeats the identical design on the two hulls that carry most of the observed series, so that the length gradient and the conditional attack rate can be read as functions of complement and layout rather than of one hull. Nothing here is fitted. The release scale is swept as a declared physical quantity (environmental_faecal_release_log10_g_per_epoch, the legacy dose_adjustment key) and reported stratified by it, because ledger item 00 forbids a posting frequency marginalised across that exponent; the shipped norwalk_gi value 4.0 is one rung and carries no privileged status. Containment is a separate axis at the shipped rung so a change in posting frequency stays attributable to transmission or to quarantine compliance rather than to their product, and none_response carries sick_call_probability_per_day 0.0, which is a no-reporting branch whose posting frequency is emitted as null rather than as a measurement. Comparators are printed and never optimised against: A4 pre-2020 reported passenger AR over postings is per-hull (classic median 0.0552, IQR 0.0415-0.0782, n=95; spirit median 0.0526, IQR 0.0418-0.0724, n=130), whereas A9 publishes no per-hull posting numerator at all, so the only posting comparators available for these hulls are the fleet-pooled interval (4.19-5.58 per 1,000 voyages) and its length-resolved rows. Resolution is a design choice and not a power calculation: 1,000 voyages at the shipped rung fix a rate near 5 per 1,000 to roughly 2-12 per 1,000, which distinguishes a per-1,000 from a per-100 regime and cannot separate A9's 4.19 from its 5.58; the 150-voyage curve cells resolve a frequency near 0.5 to about plus or minus 0.04, which is all the ladder has to do.

c1_cls_posting_curve_7d.description: Posting frequency against the declared release scale on a 7-day voyage at mid compliance. Six rungs one log apart bracket the shipped 4.0 on both sides and span the region where ledger item 00 recorded a switch on the pre-merge chain; the ladder locates where posting crosses realistic values on this hull rather than asserting a value.

c1_cls_posting_curve_12d.description: The same ladder at 12 days, thinned to three rungs. Paired with the 7-day cells this is the voyage-length gradient the expedition hull got wrong, measured on a hull whose complement and compartmentation are representative of the observed A9 denominator.

c1_cls_containment_7d.description: Quarantine compliance swept at the shipped rung and 7 days, including the no-reporting branch. Held apart from the release ladder so that a change in posting frequency is attributable to compliance or to transmission and not to their product.

c1_cls_shipped_rung_7d.description: Seed extension at the shipped rung, 7 days. Carries seeds 3200-4049 only: a run id is <pathogen>_<platform>_adj<d>_ep<n>_<surveillance>_s<seed> and holds no tier name, so the curve cell's seeds 3000-3149 at this rung are already taken and re-listing them would be either skipped by --resume or raced by two shards writing one run directory. The readout keys cells on platform, surveillance, release scale and epoch count, so this tier and its curve cell report as one 1,000-voyage cell -- the only cell compared against an observed posting probability.

c1_cls_shipped_rung_12d.description: Seed extension at the shipped rung, 12 days, seeds 3200-4049 for the same run-id reason. Together with the 7-day extension this gives the length gradient 1,000 voyages at each end, which is the precision the expedition campaign lacked when it found the gradient too shallow.
